subject: Numeric-banded discount proposal for renewal + mid-contract top-up
messages:
From: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@starlabs.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@starlabs.ai>
Date: 2025-10-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal pricing — seeking banded discount options for mid-contract growth

Hi Markus,

Quick context: we're nearing our renewal with Redwood (renewal window: Jan 2026) but expect a material mid-contract top-up in Nov for a new ML workload. Finance asked whether we can structure a banded discount schedule so that incremental capacity (and any uplift applied before co-term) gets a clearer discount path.

Key asks:
- Can you share a proposal with numeric bands (e.g., +25%, +50%, +100% of current committed capacity) and the corresponding discount off list?
- How would co-terming new topups into Jan 2026 look from an invoice and proration perspective?
- Any constraints on stacking promotional credits or one-off onboarding discounts?

We want to present a clean plan to procurement next week (target: Oct 22). Happy to jump on a short call if easier.

Thanks —
Sarah
Procurement Manager
Starlabs AI

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@starlabs.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-15T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing — seeking banded discount options for mid-contract growth

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear brief. I put together a numeric-banded approach that keeps pricing simple while preserving predictability for Starlabs and clarity for your procurement team. I attached a quick calc and a draft SOW for co-term language.

Proposal (summary):
- Base: maintain current committed capacity and current rate card (no change for existing commit).
- Band A (+25% incremental capacity over current commit): 7.5% discount on incremental tokens/instances. Billing: billed monthly; no retroactive change to base commit.
- Band B (+50% incremental): 12% discount on incremental units.
- Band C (+100% or more incremental): 18% discount on incremental units AND eligibility for a 30-day free trial of Redwood Optimize features (one-time).

Co-term and proration:
- Option 1 (immediate co-term): top-up amount prorated to Jan 31, 2026 and billed in the next invoice. This converts incremental top-up into a Jan-2026-aligned commit; discount applies pro rata for the first billing cycle.
- Option 2 (standalone top-up): treat the top-up as separate monthly usage (no commit); band discounts apply on usage thresholds but there is no co-term conversion.

Stacking rules / credits:
- Promotional onboarding credits cannot be combined with band coupons; however, promotional dollars can be applied to invoices in the same period.
- One-time onboarding discount (if approved by sales leadership) can reduce the first invoice on the top-up but will not change the long term per-unit discount band.

Next steps I recommend:
1) If you want Option 1, confirm the expected uplift volume (approx %) and the preferred co-term date (I assume Jan 31).
2) I’ll route the final numeric tables to finance/CS and get Ben to confirm invoice mechanics.
3) We can produce a canonical quote and updated SOW for procurement to sign.

Attaching: starlabs_discount_calc.xlsx (simple tier calc) and SOW-draft-starlabs.pdf (co-term clause).

If helpful, I have availability Oct 16 10am PT for a 30-min call.

Best,
Markus Klein
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal pricing — seeking banded discount options for mid-contract growth

Markus — thanks for the draft. A couple of quick operational notes from finance/CS:

- For Option 1 (immediate co-term), we need to be explicit in the quote about how the first invoice will show (line items: base commit, prorated top-up, applied discount on incremental lines). Procurement often flags ambiguity there.
- Recommend we cap Band C discount to the uplift delta vs. base commit for the first 90 days to avoid retroactive entitlement edge cases. We can remove the cap after QoQ review.
- If Starlabs requests vendor-side invoicing to match their fiscal calendar, that’s doable but requires 30 days to sync with billing pipeline.

I updated the calc sheet (see tab "ops_notes"). Ben — can you validate the proposed billing ledger entries? I think we can approve the one-time onboarding waiver of up to $12k if legal signs off.

Naomi
Director, Customer Finance & Ops
Redwood Inference
